decisions.reason: Because it builds directly on the firm’s established geospatial components business and already had its own webpage at launch, its early signals likely meet a modest aspiration level in a growing market, so management would keep it.

The building data digital twin service fits the firm’s integration and consulting capabilities and benefits from industry growth and some innovative-firm slack, though its weaker website prominence makes its continuation a bit less certain.

Authentication and identity delegation is close to the offer but less central to the firm’s distinctive geospatial positioning, so if early uptake is only modest it may fall short of aspiration somewhat, yet management would still likely retain it for now while learning.

An open GIS application development framework is strongly aligned with the firm’s open, extensible, user-centered strategy and research orientation, so management would likely view it as satisfactory enough to continue.

The identity and access service was explicitly introduced as a new GIS integration offering and complements the core platform business, so with no clear sign of failure a medium-sized innovative firm would likely keep it despite some uncertainty.
